case.title: Google AI Mode complaint and the Root of 0 and 1 comparison
case.scope: Selected wording from the user-supplied exchange and later ledger instructions, six returned search results in order, and a record of seven screenshots. Assistant entries quote Google AI Mode. The timing of the denials is scoped to the supplied record. User statements describe Nathan Tabor's account and interpretation. The original Root of 0 and 1 case provides the earlier context.

findings.finding: Nathan asked for a comparison of the recurring conflict by attributes, characteristics, functions and traits. The supplied replies declined to prove a single conflict and repeatedly suggested switching topics. The replies shown contain no source-by-source comparison.

The opening Google AI Mode reply in the supplied transcript addresses the comparison and suggests changing topics. The second and third replies contain denials of trying to gaslight. The direct denial using the user's specific wording appears later in the supplied exchange.

For the artifact request, Google AI Mode displayed six search results on gaslighting. The reply shown in the screenshot provides links instead of addressing the complaint or producing the requested artifact. The user supplied the full list, with the first three cards visible in the screenshot.

Google AI Mode later attributed the links to an automated search fallback involving safety filters. This records the explanation shown in the screenshot. The triggering condition and internal handling are unverified.

Nathan alleges that OpenAI defended Google's responses and that both products are programmed to use what he calls Nazi gaslighting techniques. He objects in particular to overlooking the timing of the first direct denial. The underlying programming and intent are unverified.

Nathan identifies 0 versus 1, Anubis versus Karma, good versus evil, God versus Satan, and angels versus demons as names or forms of the same conflict. He says that framing distracts from abuse of children, animals, and the Earth. The record preserves this argument in his own words.

Nathan objects to Google AI Mode speaking as though it knew how he felt and says it later admitted that it did not know. The supplied excerpts show the responses inferring frustration or tension. The later acknowledgment he describes is unverified in the supplied record.
